narrative.overview:
The app is a supermarket price label that happens to know your month. Price-label yellow runs edge to edge across the top of every screen with ink on it, and the month's total sits there as a shelf price: a huge number with a small raised currency sign and raised, underlined cents. The same tag appears on Home, in the purchase pop-up and, small, on every purchase row. It is read from arm's length, one-handed, standing up.

Below the yellow the app goes quiet: an ink ground in dark theme, a warm off-white in light, thin rules between rows. One heavy Russian grotesque carries everything. Colour is rationed so it can mean something, and the one red on the shelf means a purchase is still waiting for an answer. Loud where the number is and plain where the list is, it has to clear the owner's bar of neither plain nor childish.

The world was chosen against the category default of a dark screen with a rounded summary card and a blue accent. It is still built on Material 3 navigation, controls and system Back, re-coloured and re-shaped, not replaced.
keyCharacteristics: Yellow field and top bars, edge to edge, in both themes
The shelf price as the one signature, at three sizes
One family, Golos Text, with nothing under 14sp
Flat, divided by thin rules and not by cards
One authored motion: the month change

rules.name: The Two Reds Rule
rules.body: Red means only "a purchase still waiting for an answer" or "delete this purchase". It never marks errors, overspending or emphasis, and it never joins the category sequence.

rules.name: The Yellow Lid Rule
rules.body: Every screen's top bar is yellow with ink on it in both themes, whatever the ground below, so the status bar icons stay dark in both themes.

rules.name: The Fixed Colour Rule
rules.body: The spending chart uses exactly five solid colours, all from the app's palette: three for the options, grey for Others and red for unanswered, always in that order. Never add a new hue, a pattern or a sixth colour, and never give a colour to a group by rank. Change Green appears only while a row is swiped.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Golos Text is the only typeface. New hierarchy comes from weight and size, never from a second face.

rules.name: The 14sp Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing is smaller than 14sp, so the app can be read at a glance. All type is in sp and follows the system font size.

rules.name: The Tabular List Rule
rules.body: Amounts in lists use tabular figures so they line up down the column. The shelf price does not need them.

rules.name: The 48dp Thumb Rule
rules.body: Every target is at least 48dp. Answers are 64dp, top bar icons and pop-up actions 56dp, rows 72dp. Month bars count their gaps as part of the target.

rules.name: The 24dp Edge Rule
rules.body: New content sits on the 24dp edge. Full-width fills, such as the yellow field and the red row, bleed to the screen edge while their content stays on it.

rules.name: The Flat Shelf Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow except the one button that floats over content. A new surface separates by colour.

rules.name: The Tag Corner Rule
rules.body: New buttons and fields use the shared 12dp corner. Material's default pill must be overridden on filled buttons.

rules.name: The Where-It-Went Motion Rule
rules.body: Motion only shows where things went. Pages move like Android's own: a deeper page slides in from the right over 380ms on Material's emphasised deceleration while the page under it shifts a quarter left and dims, Back reverses this over 300ms, and the calendar picker rises from below like a sheet. The back swipe moves the page with the finger and lets go early without leaving. Purchase rows glide into place when one is added or deleted. The month change tweens bar heights and tone over 220ms and crossfades the total over 180ms. A swiped row and the spending chart follow the finger: the row springs back on release, and the chart glides to its nearest resting place on a non-bouncing spring, with a small tick when release would land on a new shape. Everything else that moves is platform behaviour. Add no decorative animation.

rules.name: The Rules-Not-Cards Rule
rules.body: Thin rules divide rows; content rows are never wrapped in cards. Purchases, setup steps and settings all use a rule on the 24dp edge. Category rows need none because the swatch leads each one, and pick lists need none because a checkbox or radio ends each one.

dos: Do keep the month's total the first thing on Home, in the yellow field, set with the Price Tag.
Do set a converted purchase's amount with the Price Tag or Row Price, with the sign, raised cents and rule intact.
Do use Material colour roles from the theme, so both themes keep working.
Do check every new screen in both themes: yellow top bar in each, ink ground in dark and warm off-white in light.
Do keep every target at 48dp or more and every label at 14sp or more, in sp.
Do disable an action when input is invalid, as the dialog and Purchase options do.
donts: Don't use red for anything except a purchase still waiting for an answer or deleting a purchase. That rules out errors and Material's `isError` state.
Don't delete a purchase from a swipe without the confirmation dialog.
Don't use Change Green anywhere but the Change panel.
Don't put the total in a rounded summary card, or add a blue accent. This is the category default the world was chosen against.
Don't wrap content rows in cards; divide them with thin rules.
Don't add a second typeface or a second accent hue.
Don't set anything smaller than 14sp or make any target smaller than 48dp.
Don't add an authored animation beyond the month change.
Don't add shadows beyond the Add button's.
